/ WHY
REFRACT

You bring the “what if.”
We make room for the “let’s try.”

Some ideas don’t fit inside a class period. Refract is a proposed space for PRISMS students to come together, cross disciplines, and turn an idea into something that works.

Find people who see things differently. Experiment with something unfamiliar. Build a prototype, share what you learned, and see your idea in a whole new light.

A little curiosity.
A different perspective.
Something that didn’t exist before.

/ A FEW
ANSWERS

Before you begin.

What is Refract?+

Refract is a proposed student-led PRISMS hackathon. Small teams would turn an idea into a working prototype during a focused event, then share their projects through short demonstrations and feedback.

Who can participate?+

The inaugural event is proposed for current PRISMS students, with approximately 2–5 students per team and an initial target of 30–60 participants. Final participation requirements and capacity will be determined with the school.

Does my project have to be software?+

No. The proposal includes AI, software, robotics, hardware, engineering, data science, scientific computing, and interdisciplinary projects. It is designed to bring different interests and skills together.

When and where will it happen?+

The proposed location is the PRISMS campus, using approved spaces. The date and duration are not yet confirmed. Possible formats include a full-day or extended Friday/Saturday event.

Are there prizes?+

The target is $3,000+ in total prizes, included within a broader $10,000+ cash and in-kind sponsorship goal. Prizes are not guaranteed; amounts, categories, and distribution depend on sufficient sponsorship and school approval.

How do I sign up?+

Registration has not opened. Refract is currently a proposal for school review. Participation details will be announced here once the event and registration process are approved.

How will the event be supervised?+

The organizing team plans to work with PRISMS faculty and administration on supervision, facilities, lab safety, event hours, and participation requirements. All activities and outside involvement would follow school-approved arrangements.
